card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Turn On, urrent jumps back and forth from 0 A to 320 mA, then 0 A to 1.4 A, then 0 A to 500 mA, and so on

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Does Not Turn On, urrent jumps back and forth from 0 A to 320 mA, then 0 A to 1.4 A, then 0 A to 500 mA, and so on

symptoms: current jumps 0 A to various values after power-on

claims.statement: iPhone 7 with no draw before power-on, then current bouncing between 0 A and values like 320 mA, 1.4 A, 500 mA, usually has a shorted cap on PP3V0_NAND or PP0V9_NAND.
PMIC U1801 heats when injecting through the battery connector but is not the cause.
The same pattern with PP1V8_SDRAM or PP1V1_SDRAM shorted and heat above the CPU indicates a RAM short requiring RAM replacement (advanced).

procedure: Check NAND rails PP3V0_NAND / PP0V9_NAND for shorts.
Inject voltage to find the shorted cap and remove it.
If SDRAM rails are shorted with heat above the CPU, plan RAM replacement.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
